title: Survive guildleves: hold an area, then beat the final targets
claim: Survive leves (Gamer Escape files them under the "Devotion" type) asked the party to defend an area for a set time; when the timer ran out, final targets appeared and beating them completed the leve.

sources.t: Gamer Escape: Devotion guildleves (1.0)

title: Sweet Revenge: a 5-minute hold, then two Cavern Efts
claim: Players killed Ill-tempered Pteroc for 5 minutes; after that two Cavern Efts appeared as the final targets. The leve had a 30-minute limit.

sources.t: Gamer Escape: Sweet Revenge (1.0 leve)

title: All Nine Ivies is a Stage: Bile Gnats, then Toxic Flytrap and Plasma Spark
claim: Players killed Bile Gnats until the defense timer reached zero, then a Toxic Flytrap and a Plasma Spark appeared near map 51,30. A May 2011 bug report on the official forum describes this run at 5 stars, with the Plasma Spark casting Thunder IV.

sources.t: Official forum, thread 10565 (May 2011)
Gamer Escape: All Nine Ivies is a Stage

title: Hold length for All Nine Ivies is our choice (5 minutes)
claim: No source gives the hold length for All Nine Ivies. XIVLegacy uses 5 minutes, the only Survive hold length on record (Sweet Revenge).

title: Seven Survive leves lack enough detail to rebuild
claim: For these Survive leves no source we have found records what attacked during the hold or how long it lasted, so XIVLegacy keeps them off. Keeping the Peace (10906) has no 1.0 page at all.

sources.t: Gamer Escape: Devotion guildleves (1.0)

title: Faction credit: earned from sponsored leves, spent on faction leves
claim: Finishing a guildleve sponsored by a faction gave credit with that faction. Credit was spent at the adventurers' guild to take that faction's own leves. Three factions: Broken Blade, Azeyma's Shields, and Horn and Hand (the Japanese name reads "Hand's Eye"). Patch 1.18 cut Horn and Hand rewards.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki (Japanese): ファクション, archive

title: How a faction leve ran
claim: Pick a faction and rank at the guild counter; travel to the listed aetheryte (city ones start at the aetheryte plaza); starting it places a contact NPC on the map and starts the timer; talk to them to begin; finishing may drop a chest; report back to the contact, who sends you to the aetheryte. Faction leves used the regular leve allowance.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki (Japanese): ファクションリーヴ, archive

title: Faction leve credit costs: 100 / 200 / 300 by level
claim: Level 20 faction leves cost 100 credit, level 30 cost 200, level 40 cost 300. Level 50 NM operations cost 100 each, except the third Market and Wolfsbane operations at 400. Some leves required an earlier one first.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki (Japanese): ファクションリーヴ, archive

title: Grand Company leves (patch 1.19 on)
claim: Each company's detachment officer at a camp offered one leve at a time, solo only, costing one leve allowance. Clearing another leve issued at the same place (or taking and abandoning the company leve) changed the offer. Rewards were company seals and gil; patch 1.22a added a 50-seal completion bonus and a star-based bonus (level 40: 140 seals at 1 star up to 240 at 5).

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki (Japanese): カンパニーリーヴ, archive

title: Company leve completion bonus by type
claim: Kill leves: kill at least twice the required number. Timed defense (escort) leves: keep the protected NPC's damage under a limit. Detect leves: find the crystal carrier with an emote and kill only carriers and targets. Defense leves could not end early.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki (Japanese): カンパニーリーヴ, archive

title: Leve 11004 may never have been released
claim: The client has this leve at level 100, and no 1.0 record of it exists on Gamer Escape. Treated as unreleased.

title: Leve 12484: Gamer Escape's page describes a different leve
claim: The Gamer Escape page under this title lists Quarrymill rather than Humblehearth and a different leve type, so it is not used as a source for this id.

sources.t: Gamer Escape (1.0 leve pages)

title: Weakness and Severe Weakness after being raised
claim: Getting up from KO by any means except Rebirth gives Weakness: max HP and max MP down 25%. Getting KO'd and raised again while Weakened gives Severe Weakness: max HP and MP down 50%, and physical and magic attack and defense each down 50%. The page also says Weakness slows the action gauge and lengthens recasts.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: 衰弱 (Weakness)

title: How long Weakness lasted (patch 1.18 table)
claim: In the patch 1.18 raise table, Raise (Conjurer) and Resurrect (Thaumaturge) and Return each left 3 minutes of Weakness; Raise II shortened Weakness or Severe Weakness to 1 minute; Rebirth left none. Patch 1.20 cut the raise spells down to Conjurer's Raise alone; cast as a Conjurer it doesn't weaken the target (a rank 48 trait), cast from another class it does and has a longer recast.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: 蘇生魔法 (raise spells)

title: Tier I and II of a buff replace each other; the two Spikes replace each other
claim: All buff spells' tier I and tier II versions are mutually exclusive: the later cast overwrites the earlier one, even if it is weaker (Shell over Shell II). Shock Spikes and Stygian Spikes (either tier) also overwrite each other, so players cast Stygian Spikes to get rid of Shock Spikes.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: バフ (buffs)

title: DoT spells tick about ten times; longer duration means more ticks
claim: Players counted roughly ten damage ticks from a landed DoT spell, and found that lengthening the spell's duration (Roaming Soul) raised its total damage, so duration sets the number of ticks. Early Conjurer DoTs (Shock, Choke, Drown, Burn, Frost, Rasp, I and II) each also lowered the target's magic defense against that element; Dia lowered physical defense and Bio physical attack.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: DoT (damage over time)

title: Gladiator effect durations (patch 1.20 and later)
claim: Rampart: defense up, 60 s (recast 120 s). Aegis Boon: next hit is blocked and heals you, 30 s (60 s). Shield Bash: Stun 5 s. Sentinel: damage taken down, 15 s (90 s). Riot Blade from behind: Defense Down 30 s. Outmaneuver: block rate up and TP on block, 30 s (90 s). Tempered Will removes Bind and Heavy from yourself (180 s). Goring Blade from behind: a DoT for 30 s. A rank 28 trait adds Blind to Flash. Durations as listed in the wiki's patch 1.20+ action table, which matches the in-game tooltips.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クラス/剣術士 (Gladiator)

title: Marauder effect durations (patch 1.20 and later)
claim: Foresight: parry rate up, 30 s or until one parry (60 s). Bloodbath: next hit drains HP, 30 s (60 s). Fracture after a parry: target can't use weapon skills for 8 s. Berserk and Rampage are toggles that can't be combined; taking damage resets Berserk, moving ends Rampage. Path of the Storm from behind adds Heavy. Enduring March: slower movement but immune to most debuffs, 20 s (180 s). A rank 28 trait adds Attack Down to Provoke. Durations as listed in the wiki's patch 1.20+ action table, which matches the in-game tooltips.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クラス/斧術士 (Marauder)

title: Lancer effect durations (patch 1.20 and later)
claim: Heavy Thrust: Stun 4 s if the target is targeting you. Invigorate: TP gain and no TP decay out of combat, 30 s, +15 s with a rank 28 trait (90 s). Leg Sweep combo: AoE Stun 8 s. Life Surge and Power Surge stack up to 3 times and can't be combined; Dread Spike ends them for a bigger drain. Durations as listed in the wiki's patch 1.20+ action table, which matches the in-game tooltips.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クラス/槍術士 (Lancer)

title: Pugilist effect durations (patch 1.20 and later)
claim: Featherfoot: evasion up, 30 s or until one evade (60 s). Pounce from behind: Stun 10 s. Concussive Blow from the flank: Blind 30 s. Blindside: next attack from behind crits, 60 s. Haymaker after an evade: Stun. Fists of Earth and Fists of Fire are toggles that drain MP and can't be combined. Demolish combo: Dispel. Aura Pulse combo: Slow 30 s. Taunt: the enemy is fixed on you for 5 s (60 s). Durations as listed in the wiki's patch 1.20+ action table, which matches the in-game tooltips.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クラス/格闘士 (Pugilist)

title: Archer effect durations (patch 1.20 and later)
claim: Decoy: dodge one ranged or magic attack, 60 s (90 s); a rank 16 trait adds physical. Hawk's Eye: accuracy up 15 s (90 s). Leaden Arrow: Heavy 30 s. Shadowbind: Bind 30 s. Swiftsong: party move speed up 180 s, ends when you attack or are attacked. Gloom Arrow combo: Blind 30 s. Bloodletter: DoT 30 s with a big hit at the end. Durations as listed in the wiki's patch 1.20+ action table, which matches the in-game tooltips.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クラス/弓術士 (Archer)

title: Thaumaturge effect durations (patch 1.20 and later)
claim: Parsimony, Necrogenesis, Dark Seal, Resonance and Excruciate all last 30 s (90 s recast). Blizzard: Heavy 30 s. Thundara: Stun 4 s. Blizzara: point-blank Bind 30 s. Sanguine Rite: MP from damage taken and no spell interruption, 20 s (60 s). Sleep: 60 s. Durations as listed in the wiki's patch 1.20+ action table, which matches the in-game tooltips.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クラス/呪術士 (Thaumaturge)

title: Conjurer effect durations (patch 1.20 and later)
claim: Protect and Stoneskin: 300 s each (30 s recast). Stone adds magic evasion down; Aero adds a DoT; Stonera adds Heavy; Aerora's combo adds Dispel. Cleric Stance is a toggle: attack spells +20%, healing -20%. Sacred Prism: next heal or buff becomes area-of-effect, 60 s. Shroud of Saints: enmity halved and MP regen, 20 s (180 s). Repose: Sleep. Durations as listed in the wiki's patch 1.20+ action table, which matches the in-game tooltips.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クラス/幻術士 (Conjurer)

title: Quest log: 16 story/class/side quests at once, leves counted apart
claim: Main scenario, class and side quests share one log of up to 16 active quests; finished ones leave the log. Leves don't count against it: regional leves (battle and gathering) have 8 slots and local (crafting) leves another 8. Patch 1.16a (March 2011) added abandoning a quest; before that a stuck quest held its slot for good.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クエスト (quests)

title: Quests are gated by class rank, not physical level
claim: Whether a quest is offered depends on the rank of a class (the weapon/tool skill rank), not physical level. Main scenario quests check your highest class rank; class quests check that class's rank, so you talk to the giver while on that class. If a quest doesn't appear right after ranking up, players changed zones, relogged or touched an aetheryte.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クエスト (quests)

title: Class quests at ranks 20, 30 and 36
claim: Each class guild offers class quests at ranks 20, 30 and 36: talk to the guild's receptionist while on that class at that rank. The rank 20 one also needs the rank 15 main scenario quest done. The rank 30 quest unlocks buying the guild's rank 40 skill with guild marks, the rank 36 quest the rank 50 skill.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: クエスト (quests)

title: Side quest targets always drop the quest item for players on the quest
claim: While on a side quest, the target monsters drop the quest item 100% of the time, on any class. Party members who aren't on the quest can help; only the members on the quest get the item. Givers show on the minimap with a '!' when you meet the requirement on any of your classes, even while on a crafter.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quests: added in 1.16, instanced targets from 1.17
claim: Side quests arrived in patch 1.16 (March 4, 2011). At first their target monsters gave no experience or skill points, and players not on the quest got no drops from them; patch 1.16a made the targets give experience, skill points and loot. Quests added in 1.17 (April 15, 2011) spawn their targets in an instance only the quest holder sees, and hamlet NPCs started giving quests.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: First side quests (patch 1.16, March 2011)
claim: These 19 side quests (six or seven per city) were the first batch, from patch 1.16. The wiki lists them before its patch 1.17 rows.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quests added in patch 1.17 (April 15, 2011)
claim: These side quests came with patch 1.17. Several are city tours: talk to five NPCs around town.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quests added in patch 1.17a (April 26, 2011)
claim: These side quests came with patch 1.17a. Letting Out Orion's Belt (any class, rank 10, 5,000 gil) has you hand sardine bread to four gourmets around Limsa Lominsa.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quests added in patch 1.18 (July 2011), with skill point rewards
claim: These side quests came with patch 1.18. The wiki lists a skill point reward for each, given as 'up to' a number: Sniffing Out a Profit 3,100; Sour Grapes 841; Shot Through the Heart 1,401; Secrets Unearthed 960; Freedom Isn't Free 2,820; Spores on the Brain 500; A Bitter Oil to Swallow 960. Rustproof (Ul'dah) also came in 1.18: 13,000 gil and skill points up to 1,980. One more, Gridania's To Deskunk a Beer (14,000 gil, up to 2,700), isn't in our quest list.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quests added in patch 1.19
claim: These side quests came with patch 1.19 (the wiki dates it October 5, 2011). What a Pirate Wants, Cutthroat Prices and A Slippery Stone are offered only by your starting city's adventurers' guild (Baderon, Momodi, Miounne). Call of Booty ties in with Shposhae.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quests that need a Disciple of War or Magic at the listed rank
claim: For these side quests the requirement is a fighter or sorcerer class at the quest's rank (any one of them; the shield skill counts too).

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quests any class can take
claim: These side quests need any class (crafters and gatherers included) at the listed rank. Proceed with Caution and Playing with Fire were fighter/sorcerer-only until patch 1.17 opened them to all classes.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Beryl Overboard needs Till Death Do Us Part first
claim: Beryl Overboard (Nanapiri) only appears after Till Death Do Us Part (H'lahono) is done: Nanapiri is smitten with H'lahono. Both send you to Bloodshore, so players went twice.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Have You Seen My Son runs through all three cities into Say it with Wolf Tails
claim: Have You Seen My Son starts with Imania in Limsa Lominsa, then goes to Yuyubesu at the Amajina mining company in Ul'dah, the Bomb Embers in Nanawa Mines, back to Yuyubesu, and ends with Ildy in Ul'dah's adventurers' guild. It leads into Gridania's Say it with Wolf Tails (Francis at the Wailing Barracks; needs Have You Seen My Son done): kill Knowing Gnats in the MunTuy Cellars, and Francis gives a wolf tail to take back to Imania in Limsa.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: The Ultimate Prank needs The Penultimate Prank first
claim: Nicoliaux gives both. The Penultimate Prank: eight blinking eyes from Aurora Anglers at the Humblehearth (27-31). The Ultimate Prank (rank 35, needs the first): Nicoliaux, Sylbyrt at the Carline Canopy, a Wandering Wight in the MunTuy Cellars (5-3), Sylbyrt again, Nicoliaux.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Winds of Change: city tour, then a bandit fight
claim: From Zanthael on the first floor of the Mizzenmast (near the chocobos): talk in turn to NPCs at the Limsa entrance bridge, between the Bismarck and the Coral Tower, inside the Coral Tower, at the aetheryte plaza and at the port, report back, then fight a group of sharp-eyed bandits (two plus two) in the cave northwest of Camp Bearded Rock (23-27), followed by an instanced scene with Copeli Yopeli. Reward 7,500 gil.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Quid Pro Quo: city tour, then bandits at a crash site
claim: From Peneli Zuneli at the Milvaneth Sacrarium: a chain of NPCs (Gladiators' Guild, Sapphire Avenue, Frondale's) and then bandits at a crash site northwest of Ul'dah (Thanalan map 23-28). Reward 7,500 gil.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Proceed with Caution: refill three lanterns outside Gridania
claim: From Sandre at the Greatloam Growery: inspect the '???' spots near Gridania at 29-28, 31-30 and 34-32 and pour the oil Sandre gave you into each guardian lantern. Reward Dated Dodoskin Shoes.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Playing with Fire: light three bonfires
claim: From Maroile at Stillglade Fane: inspect the '???' spots near Gridania at 15-20, 26-33 and 29-31 and use the warm pot Maroile gave you to light a fire at each.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Scrubbing the Soul: talk around town, then fight bandits
claim: From Mestonnaux at the Greatloam Growery: hear out NPCs around the city, then fight a group of sharp-eyed bandits (rank 15, two plus two) south of Camp Bentbranch (33-38) and talk in an instanced scene; report to Mestonnaux. Reward 7,500 gil.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Where the targets of several side quests are
claim: Clasping to Hope: two rank 35 Amalj'aa Lancers south of Halatali (42-29). Traumaturgy: Amalj'aa northeast of Halatali (44-25), bring back a ring. Best Flower Ever: six rank 10 dodos southeast of the Golden Bazaar. The Unheard Horizon: east of Camp Horizon (16-29). Hunting the Hunters: Ixal at Quarrymill. Food for Thought: use the cheer emote on five NPCs around Limsa, then talk to them. Stone Deaf: a Galago at Camp Tranquil (37-48). Embarrassing Excerpts: an Opo-opo in the MunTuy Cellars (7-5). A Hypocritical Oath: five antelopes; Counting Sheep: four dread wolves (both from Owl's Nest in Coerthas).

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Side quest rewards our records lack or give without amounts
claim: Gil and stack sizes from the wiki: Winds of Change 7,500 gil; Trading Tongueflaps 2,500 gil; Food for Thought 10,000 gil; Quid Pro Quo 7,500 gil; Best Flower Ever 5,000 gil; Stone Deaf 10,000 gil; Scrubbing the Soul 7,500 gil; In the Name of Science 5,000 gil; Spores on the Brain 5,000 gil; Shot Through the Heart 10,000 gil; A Hypocritical Oath 12,500 gil. Moonstruck 12 pineapple juice; Seashells by the Seashore 12 boiled crayfish; Fishing for Answers 50 crab balls; Of Archons and Muses 10 orange juice; The Unheard Horizon 100 wind shards; Sanguine Studies 12 blood currant tarts; Clasping to Hope 6 Ironhide Unguent; Traumaturgy 6 Ironwill Unguent; Hearing Confession 12 flatbread; Embarrassing Excerpts 20 lightning crystals; A Forbidden Love 12 bronze azagai; Last Respects 20 earth crystals; Hunting the Hunters 100 iron arrows; Counting Sheep 12 grilled dodo; Sour Grapes 100 water shards; Sniffing Out a Profit 2 Grade 4 Dark Matter; Secrets Unearthed 5 of tekkō (鉄鋼, 'steel'; the client has no item by that name, so likely Steel Ingots); Freedom Isn't Free Spiked Knuckles; A Bitter Oil to Swallow a Dated Oiled Bronze Hatchet.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: サブクエスト (side quests)

title: Job quests (patch 1.21): unlock at main class 30 and a second class 15
claim: Jobs came with patch 1.21. Each job has six quests. The first (the job quest proper) needs the main class at level 30 and a set second class at 15; it gives the job's soul crystal, the first job action and a copy of The Keeper's Hymn (meant for a future stat reset; it stacks, one per job). The rest unlock at levels 35, 40, 45 (two quests: one action, one collecting four artifact pieces) and 50 (artifact body plus the fifth action), checked against the main class level. After unlocking, accept, fight and report as the job: fights done as a class or another job don't count. The level 45 collection quest has four chests in the field or in instanced raids; with the quest active they show a '!' and any class or job can open them. The level 50 quest is a full-party fight.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ジョブクエスト (job quests)

title: Paladin quests: Lulutsu, then Jenlyns
claim: 1 Paladin's Pledge: Lulutsu at the Gladiators' Guild, Ul'dah (5,5); Gladiator 30 and Conjurer 15; kill a few monsters south of Camp Horizon; gives Cover. 2 Honor Lost (35): Jenlyns on Ul'dah's upper level (6,5), around the central atrium; an Alux in the MunTuy Cellars, 2-3 players; gives Divine Veil. 3 Power Struggles (40): NM Old Six-arms south of Cedarwood, 2-3 players; Holy Succor. 4 Poisoned Hearts (45): artifact chests at Aurum Vale (Camp Ever Lakes), Natalan (Camp Dragonhead), the cave north of Camp Brittlebark and the cave northeast of Camp Crimson Bark; gives Gallant legs, hands, feet and head. 5 Parley on High Ground (45): a fight north of Ul'dah (southeast of Nanawa Mines), 4+ players; Spirits Within. 6 Keeping the Oath (50): fight an ogre and ahrimans southeast of Camp Bluefog; Gallant body and Hallowed Ground.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ジョブクエスト (job quests)

title: Warrior quests: Neale, then Curious Gorge
claim: 1 Pride and Duty: Neale at the Marauders' Guild, Limsa Lominsa lower decks (4,7); Marauder 30 and Gladiator 15; talk to Curious Gorge, then kill antlings just north of him; gives Vengeance. Curious Gorge stands in a cave east of the Scorpion Keep gate south of Camp Horizon, under Nophica's Wells (Western Thanalan 15,33). 2 Embracing the Beast (35): NM Sirocco, soloable; Antagonize. 3 Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar (40): canyon condors north of the Silver Bazaar, soloable; Collusion. 4 Looking the Part (45): chests in Cutter's Cry (east of Camp Bluefog), Natalan (east of Camp Dragonhead), in Turning Leaf and in the tower before Widow Cliffs southeast of Camp Bearded Rock; Fighter's legs, hands, feet, head. 5 Proof is in the Pudding (45): kill Audhumbla (a buffalo) in the cave southeast of Camp Iron Lake, about 4 players; Steel Cyclone. 6 How to Quit You (50): a full-party fight at the Silver Bazaar; Fighter's body and Mighty Strikes.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ジョブクエスト (job quests)

title: Monk quests: Gagaruna, Erik, Widargelt
claim: 1 Brother from Another Mother: Gagaruna at the Pugilists' Guild, Ul'dah (5,4); Pugilist 30 and Lancer 15; kill imps southwest of Camp Drybone (west of Halatali); gives Shoulder Tackle. 2 Insulted Intelligence (35): Erik, opposite Ul'dah's chocobo stable (7,3); NM Gluttonous Gertrude south of Cedarwood, solo or 2; Spinning Heel. 3 The Pursuit of Power (40): NM Prince of Pestilence in the MunTuy Cellars, solo or 2; Fists of Wind. 4 Good Vibrations (45): Apep at the north edge of Camp Horizon's area, 3-4 players, tougher than it looks; Dragon Kick. 5 Five Easy Pieces (45): from Widargelt in Little Ala Mhigo south of Camp Drybone (Eastern Thanalan 38,31); chests in Dzemael Darkhold's drake room, U'Ghamaro Mines, in Turning Leaf and south of Ul'dah's east gate; Temple hands, legs, head, feet. 6 Return of the King...of Ruin (50): Erik; a full-party fight in Mor Dhona; Temple body and Hundred Fists.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ジョブクエスト (job quests)

title: Dragoon quests: Haurtefert, then Alberic
claim: 1 Eye of the Dragon: Haurtefert at the Lancers' Guild, Gridania (8,2); Lancer 30 and Pugilist 15; kill crabs west of Nine Ivies; gives Jump. 2 Lance of Fury (35): Alberic before the gate of Ishgard west of Camp Dragonhead (Coerthas Central Highlands 35,18); NM Bomb Baron in Cassiopeia Hollow, solo or 2; Disembowel. 3 Unfading Scars (40): NM Spitfire southwest of Camp Glory, 2 players; Elusive Jump. 4 Double Dragoon (45): chests at Aurum Vale, the cave north of Camp Brittlebark (by the Singing Shards), U'Ghamaro Mines and the cave north of Camp Bluefog; Drachen legs, feet, hands, head. 5 Fatal Seduction (45): Stollenwurm south of Camp Riversmeet, 3+ players; Ring of Talons. 6 Into the Dragon's Maw (50): a fight before the bridge from Camp Dragonhead toward Camp Glory; Drachen body and Dragonfire Dive.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ジョブクエスト (job quests)

title: Bard quests: Georjeaux, then Jehantel
claim: 1 A Song of Bards and Bowmen: Georjeaux at the Archers' Guild, Gridania (8,5); Archer 30 and Conjurer 15; fight Qiqirn at the east map edge from Camp Tranquil (46-48, north of the Rootslake); gives Ballad of Magi. 2 The Archer's Anthem (35): Jehantel in the South Shroud (38,48), up the slope east of Camp Tranquil; NM Bardi west of Nanawa Mines, 2-3 players; Minuet of Rigor. 3 Bard's-Eye View (40): NM Phaia at Humblehearth, 2-3 players; Paeon of War. 4 Doing It the Bard Way (45): Ixal and wolves north of Hyrstmill, 4+; Rain of Death. 5 Pieces of the Past (45): chests in Cutter's Cry, Zahar'ak (Camp Broken Water), in Turning Leaf and in the cave south of Camp Iron Lake; Choral legs, hands, feet, head. 6 Requiem for the Fallen (50): a fight before the bridge from Camp Dragonhead toward Camp Glory; Choral body and Battle Voice.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ジョブクエスト (job quests)

title: White Mage quests: Soileine, then Raya-O-Senna
claim: 1 Seeds of Initiative: Soileine at the Conjurers' Guild, Gridania (2,1); Conjurer 30 and Gladiator 15; kill mitelings at the west end of the MunTuy Cellars (4-5); gives Presence of Mind. 2 When Sheep Attack (35): Raya-O-Senna in a cave in the North Shroud (15,22), west of Emerald Moss; NM Downy Dunstan, solo or 2; Regen. 3 Lost in Rage (40): NM Cactuar Jack southwest of Camp Horizon, 2-3; Esuna. 4 The Wheel of Disaster (45): Rowland of the 99 Blades and bandits on the bridge south of Camp Bearded Rock, 3-4; Holy. 5 In Search of Succor (45): chests in Dzemael Darkhold's drake room, Zahar'ak (right of the second gate), in Turning Leaf and the southeast end of Bloodshore; Healer's legs, hands, feet, head. 6 The Chorus of Cataclysm (50): a fight with elementals at Sorrel Haven; the way there is dangerous; Healer's body and Benediction.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ジョブクエスト (job quests)

title: Black Mage quests: Yayake, Lalai, then the Western Thanalan cave
claim: 1 Hearing Voices: Yayake at the Thaumaturges' Guild, Ul'dah (4,5); Thaumaturge 30 and Pugilist 15; kill gnats by the entrance of Copperbell Mines; gives Convert. 2 A Time to Kill (35): Lalai in Ul'dah (7,6); NM Daddy Longlegs west of Nophica's Wells, 3-4; Freeze. 3 International Relations (40): Whitetalon south of Camp Bald Knoll, about 4; Flare. 4 The Voidgate Breathes Gloomy (45): Dozol Meloc in a cave in Western Thanalan (11,28): take the path down toward the Ferry Docks and go east through the cave; search a chest in Turning Leaf, with wolves nearby; Sleepga. 5 Gearing Up (45): 269th Order Mendicant Da Za in the same cave; chests at Aurum Vale, a tower north of Camp Riversmeet, the cave west of Camp Brittlebark and the cave south of Camp Broken Water; Wizard's legs, hands, feet, head. 6 Always Bet on Black (50): a fight at Nald's Reflection northeast of Camp Broken Water against a Batraal-like enemy; Wizard's body and Burst.

title: Enmity since patch 1.18: cumulative, with a meter
claim: Patch 1.18 replaced the old enmity system with a simple cumulative one: damage and debuffs add enmity directly, heals and buffs on engaged players add it indirectly, both in proportion to the amount. A player who can't act for a while (KO) has their enmity reset. An icon left of the monster's HP bar shows your share: none (not engaged with you), green, orange, red, and flashing red when it targets you. Player tests in 1.20b put the enmity potion and the calming potion at about 190 each way and Chameleon at about -760.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ヘイト (enmity)

title: Return: 15-minute recast, durability loss when used while KO'd
claim: Return is in the main menu for every class. Used normally it has a 15-minute recast and no cost. Used while KO'd it has no recast, but every equipped item loses durability: 10% at skill rank 20 and up, 5% at ranks 10-19, none below 10 (patch 1.18; 1.18b eased the low-rank loss). Before 1.18 it cost anima and nothing when KO'd. During a regional leve or behest the start aetheryte is the temporary home point, and in an instanced raid the dungeon's start. Patch 1.22 added the inn as a home point.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: デジョン (Return)

title: Battle regimens were suspended in patch 1.19
claim: Battle regimens (party members queue actions on one target, then trigger them as a chain for an extra effect: physical or magic resistance down, slower casting, TP penalties, damage up) were frozen in patch 1.19 with no date to return, so they don't exist in 1.23b. The wiki notes A Realm Reborn replaced them with Limit Break.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: バトルレジメン (battle regimen)

title: Repair rules from patch 1.19 on
claim: Since 1.19 a repair NPC is posted at every camp as well as in the cities and restores worn gear to 99% for a flat fee by item level: 100 gil (levels 1-10), 500 (11-20), 1,000 (21-30), 2,100 (31-40), 5,000 (41-50). Items lose no performance from 100% down to 1%; at 0% they are broken and give no stats (materia included). A yellow icon warns at 10% or less, a red one when broken. Dark matter is the only repair material: grade 1-5 sold for 50, 300, 700, 1,500 and 3,500 gil (1.19), grade 6 added in 1.20 for level 50+ gear. 1.20 let NPCs repair accessories; 1.20a added repair requests for equipped gear at 100-500 gil plus the matching dark matter grade, paid by the requester.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: 修理 (repair)

title: Leve allowances since patch 1.19: 4 every 12 hours, up to 99
claim: Patch 1.19 replaced the 36-hour refresh with allowances: 4 every 12 real hours, stockpiled up to 99, shared by regional, local and faction leves (and Grand Company leves). The leve counter list also refreshes whenever you complete or fail a leve. A failed leve can be retried for one allowance, from the journal, an aetheryte or the counter. 1.19a replaced leve exchange with a history evaluation that issues one leve based on your last eight completed. Before 1.19: a server-wide refresh every 36 hours, 8 regional and 8 local leves at a time.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ギルドリーヴ (guildleves)

title: Leve difficulty: five levels picked at the aetheryte
claim: After choosing a leve at the aetheryte you pick a difficulty for your party size, from one star (kogun funtō, 孤軍奮闘: solo) to five (jinkai senjutsu, 人海戦術). Higher difficulty can raise the reward and the treasure chest's contents. In a party, a member holding the same leve can join with Leve Link (better chest odds, difficulty and completion rewards); a member without it joins through Leve Share. The completion reward goes to the leve's owner.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: ギルドリーヴ (guildleves)

title: Behests: every 30 minutes at regional leve camps
claim: A behest officer appears at camps in La Noscea, Thanalan and the Black Shroud (not Coerthas or Mor Dhona) at :00 and :30 real time and calls for players every minute. Patch 1.17 timings: 8 players max (was 15), every 30 minutes (was hourly), sign-up 3 minutes (was 5), 20-minute limit (was 30), 5 minutes to collect the reward (was 10). Kill every target before time runs out, then talk to the officer for the reward. Monsters are still claimed per party. 1.18 scaled the monsters by participant count and rank again, added skill points on completion with a speed bonus, cut the gil, added a bonus for regions whose behests had gone unrun or failed, and added a cooldown; 1.19 changed it so only players who ran the previous behest wait two extra minutes. Leaving the area drops you from the behest.

title: Field NMs: time and weather windows, short random repops
claim: Field NMs spawn when their time-of-day and weather conditions are met, with no lottery: during the window they pop at random intervals and despawn when it ends. Repop after a kill is random, from right away to about 5 minutes (a few over 10). An NM claimed during its window stays until the claim is dropped, even past the window. Players outside the party can't heal those fighting it. Drops go to a random party member, as with normal monsters.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: NM (notorious monsters)

title: Which field NMs came when
claim: December 2010: Uraeus (Coerthas, Camp Dragonhead), Great Buffalo (La Noscea, Camp Bald Knoll), Dodore (Mor Dhona, Camp Brittlebark), Elder Mosshorn (Nophica's Wells), and an NM at Treespeak. April 2011 (aimed at parties around rank 30): Bomb Baron and Unknown Soldier (Cassiopeia Hollow), Barometz and Slippery Sykes (near Camp Bloodshore), Gluttonous Gertrude and Old Six-arms (Cedarwood), Pyrausta and Nest Commander (Camp Horizon), Daddy Longlegs (Copperbell Mines), Cactuar Jack (Nophica's Wells), Bardi (Nanawa Mines), Prince of Pestilence (MunTuy Cellars), Sirocco and Phaia (Humblehearth area), Jackanapes and Queen Bolete (Camp Tranquil), Downy Dunstan and Spitfire (Camp Glory), and others. October 2011 (1.19): NMs in Western Thanalan, Shposhae (Giant Remora among them), Zahar'ak and U'Ghamaro (Third Order Patriarch Zu Ga).

title: Faction NM leves come in three stages
claim: Each faction NM leve (Operation Market, the Tarpe Uishka chase, Operation Wolfsbane) is three leves in a row costing 100, 100 and 400 faction credits; after clearing all three, the third alone can be repeated for 400. The final chest can hold an Allagan stone (otherwise a few crystals), but only for the player who started the leve and members who Leve Linked with the same leve; helpers through Leve Share get crystals and a few thousand gil. Each player opens their own chest.

title: Crafting: what each unstable element does
claim: When an element turns unstable during synthesis: ice lowers progress a little and makes sparks worse; lightning lowers progress; earth raises durability loss a little and makes sparks worse; wind raises durability loss; water lowers quality gain a little and makes sparks worse; fire lowers quality gain. Sparks lower the success rate and raise durability loss on elemental bursts and finishing work. The light orb's color hints at stability: white is safest, rainbow riskiest but best for quality.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: 製作 (synthesis)

title: Main tool versus off-hand tool in synthesis
claim: Most recipes give a different high-quality result depending on the tool: the main tool tends to make +1/+2 items, the off-hand tool more items per synthesis (for example 16 instead of 12). Dyeing a finished item never lowers its quality and keeps its materia, but a dyed item can't be re-dyed or undyed; re-forging an item into a variant (adding material) is a normal synthesis and loses materia.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: 製作 (synthesis)

title: Gathering point grades by camp
claim: Grade 1 to 5 gathering areas: La Noscea Bearded Rock, Skull Valley, Bloodshore, Cedarwood, Iron Lake; Thanalan Black Brush, Drybone, Horizon, Nophica's Wells, Halatali; Black Shroud Bentbranch, Emerald Moss, Tranquil, Humblehearth, Treespeak; Coerthas grade 4 Camp Glory and grade 5 Camp Dragonhead. Fishing once had grade 6+ spots; patch 1.18 removed them.

sources.t: FF14 Online Wiki: 採集 (gathering)

title: Which stats help which gatherer
claim: Official answer quoted on the wiki: STR makes the right angle easier to read when logging, VIT the right strength when mining, DEX the right rod motion when fishing; INT raises botanists' yield, MND miners', PIE fishers'. Gathering-gear stats: one lowers Remainder loss with the main tool or raises success with the off-hand, one raises attempts and fish bites, one raises the chance of high quality. Patch 1.19 made gathered items either normal or +3 quality and eased the success drop from gathering for a long time.

title: Raging Strike: stacks on Light Shot hits, ends on any miss
claim: Archer's Raging Strike (level 14, 60 s recast) raises attack power each time Light Shot hits while it is active, to a maximum of three stacks. The effect ends when an attack misses, not only when a Light Shot misses. The level 36 trait Enhanced Raging Strike makes the effect 50% stronger.

claim: Both Heavy Shot and Piercing Arrow have to be used from at least 8 yalms away from the target to count as the start of a combo. Heavy Shot opens Leaden Arrow and Quick Nock; Piercing Arrow opens Shadowbind and Gloom Arrow.

title: Actions are gated by class, not by weapon type
claim: From patch 1.20 each action is either exclusive to the class that learns it or can be set by any Disciple of War class (other kinds cover all combat classes or all Disciples of Magic). The class in use is set by the equipped weapon, and up to 10 actions from other classes can be set.

title: Combos count only for the owning class and waive the follow-up's TP
claim: A weaponskill combo only counts when the weaponskill is used by the class or job it belongs to. A successful combo gives the listed bonus and the follow-up weaponskill costs no TP.
